//: gamepanel and gamebroker (in src/) are installed editable into .venv by `uv sync`
(pyproject.toml at the root) - that is what resolves `import gamepanel...`/`import
gamebroker...` in the editor, along with Flask. Without it app.py opens with 'Import
"flask" could not be resolved' and the warning stays there forever, teaching people
pythonPlatform=Linux because that is where the panel runs. Without it the editor
analyzes the Windows stdlib and reports fcntl.ioctl, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, os.setsid,
pty.openpty and signal.SIGHUP as nonexistent - precisely the block that app.py already
guards with try/except ImportError so it keeps working outside Linux.
The .venv is a DEVELOPMENT TOOL, not a panel dependency. In production the
container installs python3-flask through apt and downloads no package from anywhere -
see CLAUDE.md. What decides what the panel may import is still
